page.layout: One page of running text, with a quotation set off by » marks at the start of each line. A marginal note in the left margin reads "Augustinus", opposite the paragraph beginning "Eam in sententiam". The paragraph "Quare idem" runs on to the foot of the page.

main_text.p: » non poterat. Nunc autem idem arbitrium co- » versum est; non eversum: & donatum est ei » aliter sapere, aliter agere; & incolumitatem » suam, non in se, sed in Medico, collocare. Quia » necdum perfectâ utitur sanitate: ut ea, quæ » ei nocuerunt, nequeant jam nocere; aut ab in- » salubribus possit jam, suis viribus, temperare. » Proinde homo, qui in libero arbitrio fuit ma- » lus; in ipso libero arbitrio factus est bonus: sed » per se malus; per Deum bonus, &c. Vide etiam sequentia, confirmata evidente Dei verbo. Manet ergo liberum arbitrium post lapsum: ita ut, qui credit, aut assentitur, credat & assentiatur voles æque, ac qui non credit, & non assentitur.

AugustinusEam in sententiam Augustinus, libro contra eosdem: Consentire vocationi, aut non-consentire, propriæ voluntatis est. Quod nos, uti nec alterum, non negamus: Ut velimus, suum esse voluit, & nostrum: suâ, vocando; (efficaciter putàs non extrinsecus tantùm) nostrum, sequendo. Ex hypothesi enim loquitur, positæ, & negatæ sequelæ.

page.notes: The left margin carries a printed ornament (a pointing hand) above the note "Augusti-nus.", which is not text and is left out. The lines of the quotation each begin with a printed » mark, which is kept. "suâ" (line 9 of the quotation area, in "suâ, vocando") is a doubtful reading: the printed word looks like "fuu" and was read as "suâ"; "suu" may be intended. "voles" and "putàs" are copied as printed. The printed hyphen in "prio-res" is kept as printed. The paragraph continues on the next page.
